problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+5x{y}^{′}+3y=x{e}^{x},\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=\frac{A}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{B}{x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation. 

*Hint: You may wish to make use of the following results:* 

$$
\int {x}^{3}{e}^{x}\text{d}x=({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+6x-6){e}^{x}+C
$$

and

$$
\int x{e}^{x}\text{d}x=(x-1){e}^{x}+C
$$
worked_solution:
First, we reduce the differential equation to the form

$$
{y}^{″}+P(x){y}^{′}+Q(x)y=f(x).
$$

So, we divide both sides of the given equation by ${x}^{2}.$ We get

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{5}{x}{y}^{′}+\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}y=\frac{{e}^{x}}{x}.
$$

We notice that the forcing term $f(x)=\frac{{e}^{x}}{x}.$ Additionally, we're given the fundamental solutions:

$$
{y}_{1}(x)=\frac{1}{{x}^{3}},\,{y}_{2}(x)=\frac{1}{x}
$$

First, let's compute the Wronskian:

$$
\begin{aligned}W({y}_{1},{y}_{2}) & =|\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{1}^{′} & {y}_{2}^{′}\end{aligned}| \\  & ={y}_{1}{y}_{2}^{′}-{y}_{1}^{′}{y}_{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}{(\frac{1}{x})}^{′}-{(\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})}^{′}\frac{1}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}(-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})-(-\frac{3}{{x}^{4}})\frac{1}{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{5}} \\  & =\frac{2}{{x}^{5}}\ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

Since the Wronskian is not equal to zero, this confirms that the functions  ${y}_{1}(x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)$ are independent. 

According to the method of variation of parameters, the particular solution of the differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}(x) & ={y}_{1}(x)u(x)+{y}_{2}(x)v(x),\end{aligned}
$$

where

$$
\begin{aligned}u(x) & =-\int \frac{f(x){y}_{2}(x)}{W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2}\int {x}^{3}{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{2}({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+6x-6){e}^{x}, \\ v(x) & =\int \frac{f(x){y}_{1}(x)}{W({y}_{1},{y}_{2})}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}\int x{e}^{x}\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{2}(x-1){e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}(x) & ={y}_{1}(x)u(x)+{y}_{2}(x)v(x) \\  & =(\frac{1}{{x}^{3}})(-\frac{1}{2}({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+6x-6){e}^{x})+(\frac{1}{x})(\frac{1}{2}(x-1){e}^{x}) \\  & =(-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2x}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2x}){e}^{x} \\  & =(\frac{1}{x}-\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{3}{{x}^{3}}){e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$
